chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Al-Husayn ibn Abi Uthman, from Khalid al-Jawwan, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is befitting for one of you, when he wears a new garment, to pass his hand over it and say: All praise is to Allah, Who clothed me with what I cover my nakedness with, and beautify myself with among people, and adorn myself with among them.'

key_terms.يُمِرَّ يَدَهُ: to pass his hand (over the garment)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication when wearing new clothes in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) establishes the spiritual etiquette of gratitude (shukr) upon acquiring new garments, linking physical adornment to divine provision. The supplication highlights the dual purpose of clothing: fulfilling the religious obligation of covering one's 'awrah' and enhancing social dignity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing modesty with aesthetic appreciation. This practice transforms a mundane act into an act of worship by acknowledging Allah as the ultimate source of beauty and modesty.
